title: SpaceX Is About to Become the Biggest IPO in History. Indian Tech Workers Should Pay Attention.
excerpt: With $250 billion in demand and a $1.77 trillion valuation, the SpaceX listing will reshape the market conditions that underpin Indian American wealth in tech.
body:
The largest initial public offering in stock market history is about to happen, and if you work in tech, hold stock-based compensation, or manage a 401(k) heavy on growth funds, it is about to reshape the landscape around you.

Elon Musk's SpaceX has drawn more than $250 billion in investor demand for its upcoming IPO — roughly four times the $75 billion the company is seeking to raise. The deal is expected to price on Thursday afternoon, with trading on Nasdaq beginning Friday. At a fixed price of $135 per share, the company would be valued at approximately $1.77 trillion, making it one of the most valuable publicly traded companies from day one.

Morgan Stanley is leading the roadshow. On Tuesday, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and finance chief Bret Johnsen hosted a lunch with roughly 300 institutional investors in midtown Manhattan. Musk himself briefly joined some Zoom calls with potential buyers. Long-only funds — the patient, endowment-style capital — have submitted what sources describe as "sizable orders."

## Why This Matters to Every Indian Professional in America

Indian Americans are disproportionately concentrated in the technology sector — in engineering, product management, and data science roles at exactly the kind of companies that orbit the SpaceX ecosystem. Thousands hold equity grants at firms that supply SpaceX or compete in adjacent markets. The IPO creates a gravitational pull on capital that will be felt across the entire tech industry.

Here is the immediate concern: the market is already volatile. The Nasdaq posted its steepest single-day decline in more than a year last Friday, and analysts have speculated that one contributing factor is investors liquidating existing positions to free up cash for SpaceX shares. If you hold concentrated tech equity — through RSUs, ISOs, or a growth-tilted 401(k) — the SpaceX IPO may already be affecting your portfolio, even if you never buy a single share.

The broader IPO pipeline compounds the pressure. Anthropic and OpenAI are both expected to go public in coming months. BCA Research strategists have warned that the coming wave of mega IPOs "may dampen forward market returns, mute further multiple expansion, and possibly interrupt sector trends." Ron Albahary, chief investment officer at wealth management firm LNW, has flagged what he calls an "impending chokepoint" — the risk that the market simply cannot absorb this much new stock supply without diluting valuations elsewhere.

## The Numbers Behind the Frenzy

SpaceX reported 2025 revenue of $18.67 billion, up 33 percent year-over-year. Its Starlink satellite internet business has become the dominant revenue engine, with more than 4 million subscribers globally. The company has also begun positioning AI-powered data services as a growth vertical.

At the proposed $1.77 trillion valuation, SpaceX would trade at nearly 100 times trailing revenue — a multiple that even by tech standards is extraordinary. For context, Nvidia trades at roughly 35 times revenue, and Apple at about 9 times.

SpaceX has reserved an unprecedented 30 percent of the offering for retail investors, roughly three times the typical allocation. A Japanese tranche was upsized 25 percent before the roadshow even finished. The signal is clear: this is designed to be a cultural event as much as a financial one.

## What NRI Investors Should Watch

For Indian-origin professionals in the United States, the SpaceX IPO is a stress test for the market conditions that underpin their financial lives. Rising interest rates, oil price volatility driven by the Iran conflict, and sticky services inflation have already squeezed the environment for growth equities. Adding $75 billion in new issuance to a market that is already narrow in breadth — concentrated in a handful of mega-cap names — introduces real risk.

The prudent move, according to multiple analysts, is to reassess portfolio concentration. If your wealth is heavily tied to tech sector equity, the next six months of mega IPOs may be the moment to diversify into defensive sectors, dividend-paying stocks, or India-linked investment opportunities where valuations remain more grounded.

The SpaceX IPO prices Thursday. Whether you participate or not, its ripple effects will be felt in every corner of the market where Indian American wealth is concentrated.
